question: Which wastewater plants should Horton call first?
html:
Horton should call New Haven East Shore, Hartford WPCF and Norwalk WPCF first. Each has a project on Connecticut's fundable list and high fit scores (98, 96, 95). MWRA Deer Island and Bridgeport Westside come next (CET wastewater-plant targets).

First five calls

RankPlantFlow (MGD)Fundable lead projectHorton fit
1New Haven East Shore STP40$82M wet-weather/odor control, FY2798
2Hartford WPCF (MDC)60$24.3M sludge screening/equalization, FY26-2796
3Norwalk WPCF18$26M final settling tanks, FY2795
4MWRA Deer Islandnot shown$289M Clarifier #2, 2026 IUP94
5Bridgeport Westside30not shown in extract93

(CET wastewater-plant targets; flows from EPA wastewater-plant compliance)

Why this order

  • Home-state, fundable money. The top three are Connecticut plants with Table 2 / Category I projects, which is the fundable list. Table 3 items are only requests eligible for first-come reserves. Treat these as softer:
  • New Haven's $19.2M process-air compressors
  • Hartford's $31.6M Island Road and Hog Brook pump stations
  • Norwalk's $48M aeration request

(CET wastewater-plant targets)

  • Cross-sell fit. Norwalk's aeration is the plant's largest energy load. That makes it the clearest Horton electrical plus NuWave efficiency pairing.
  • Deer Island is a different pitch. The plant already self-generates 26% of its electricity. The angle is electrical subcontracting plus storage and efficiency, not solar.
  • The growth plan agrees. Phase 1 points Horton at 62 funded or requested projects, led by New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk (CET growth plan).

Permit and inspection signals

These are public status flags only, not a compliance view (EPA wastewater-plant compliance, Nov 2, 2026):

  • Bridgeport Westside: permit admin-continued since Jun 30, 2024. It shows 12 quarters of noncompliance, 1 significant, and was last inspected 710 days ago. This plant may have near-term work not yet on the funding lists (est.).
  • Norwalk: permit expired Mar 31, 2026.
  • Hartford and New Haven: permits admin-continued since 2020 and 2021.

Gaps

  • Bridgeport Westside project and value: truncated in the extract. Pull the full target record before ranking it against Deer Island.
  • New Haven pipeline value: also truncated. Hartford's pipeline value is $105.7M and Norwalk's is $76.5M.
  • Timing: the data shows no bid dates or general-contractor awards. Owner procurement calendars would show which call is most time-sensitive.
  • Rhode Island: items come from a June 2026 draft list. Only its Table 2 rows are proposed for funding.

Next actions

  1. Book meetings with the Greater New Haven WPCA, MDC and Norwalk before FY27 awards. Lead with the fundable projects and keep the Table 3 requests as follow-ons.
  2. Build a joint Horton and NuWave aeration-efficiency pitch for Norwalk's $48M request.
  3. Pull the full Bridgeport Westside and New Haven target records, then re-rank positions 4 and 5.
  4. Map the general contractors on Deer Island Clarifier #2 so Horton can position as electrical subcontractor.
